newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour wants high corporate profits - Blair.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour wants high corporate profits - Blair.

text.p: Britain's Labour party is committed to high profits as the key to rising investment and living standards, Opposition leader Tony Blair said on Monday.

In a business-friendly speech to City leaders, Blair said Labour would look at the impact of the tax and financial system on incentives for long-term investment, including a Confederation of British Industry proposal for a two-tier capital gains tax.
"Firms invest to make money and over the decades, poor returns have probably been the biggest single explanation for the UK's poor investment record," Blair said.

"Monopoly profits are of course unacceptable, but companies earning profits in a competitive market place are a central plank of any strategy to raise investment and living standards. This means maintaining a high share of profits in a competitive economy," the Labour leader said.
Blair reaffirmed that a Labour government would have an explicit target for low and stable inflation and adhere to strict rules on borrowing and spending.

"We will also reform the Bank of England to ensure that decision-making on monetary policy is free from short-term political manipulation. In this way we will help keep down the cost of capital and improve the prospects for profitable investment," Blair said.
